New Relic's logging agent had a bug that lost a good portion of our logs for a few months last year. Support were extremely lethargic about diagnosing, and once they found it was their bug, weren't apologetic. We dropped them and moved to DD for logging.
When they changed their billing to be per user our bill went up 20x for no additional value... APM hasn't seen a single new feature in the 5 years I have used it.

Removal of development mode & support. The 'improved' price model. Their new UI is buggy as hell and they refuse to fix it. Every month or so you get a new interface that is objectively worse than what it is supposed to replace.

New Relic wants to capture as much data as possible so that they can charge you as much as possible. I run a small environment (~20 small VMs) and we quickly went over the 100GB monthly free plan just with APM Metrics... support/community was not helpful.
Reminds me of when they intentionally enabled JFR on every single java process. Roughly sextupled our ingest (and associated costs) until we got it shut back off.
New Relic is already one of the most expensive items in our budget. Last year, I had to tell a producer 'yeah, our SaaS that monitors our servers is more expensive than the servers themselves.'
Setting NEW_RELIC_APPLICATION_LOGGING_ENABLED=false and NEW_RELIC_APPLICATION_LOGGING_FORWARDING_ENABLED=false disables the newly-default automatic log collection.
I love NewRelic, but their pricing always baffled me. When we added it to our QA, UAT, and Staging envs, they started wanting to bill us as if we had 3x as many 'production' environments.
We also run our infrastructure with redundancy, so we got billed for every region & availability zone, they wanted it to be crazy expensive.

They don’t care that much about open source agent, but they do care about where the server is... there is still a huge underserved market for on-premise APMs, and those you can buy aren’t nearly as good as New Relic.

I've long preferred New Relic as well - it always seemed the most natural to use; the information that was important was easy to find... I've also had issues with New Relic - constant problems with metric names exploding.

This is the exact same situation my company finds itself in. We are stuck with it because they have decent APM metrics for .NET Java and JavaScript... The new UI is pretty difficult to use and way too bright.

I used New Relic for the first time at my current job, and while the service it provides to our team is invaluable, the UI is slow and very confusing; I can never remember what button or menu to click to get to where I need to go.
currently using NR, but it's slow, expensive and the in-cluster collection services are frustratingly fragile.

New Relic is especially slow because of the added latency of the trans-oceanic network hop [for non-US users]. The developers generally avoid it in their day-to-day work, which defeats the purpose entirely.
